lines.en: From Row Seven to the Stage
lines.zh: 从第七排到台上

lines.en: Two years later, his independent studio held its first arena show.
lines.zh: 两年后，他的独立工作室办了第一场万人演唱会。

lines.en: Again, on the last encore, he suddenly stopped the band. The arena went silent; tens of thousands held their breath — every longtime fan knew what was coming.
lines.zh: 还是唱到最后一首安可，他忽然让乐队停下。全场安静，几万人屏息——所有老粉都知道要发生什么了。

lines.en: But this time, he didn't look toward row seven.
lines.zh: 可这一次，他没有看向第七排。

lines.en: He turned around and reached a hand toward the back of the stage — and you walked out from the wings and took it.
lines.zh: 他转过身，对着舞台后方伸出手——你从侧台走出来，牵住了他。

lines.en: "I used to confess to the person in row seven," he told the whole arena, smiling, but his eyes only on you. "Now, I've invited her up on stage."
lines.zh: "以前我对第七排的人告白，"他对着全场笑，眼睛却只看你，"现在，我请她上台了。"

lines.en: A galaxy of light rose for the two of you. As the intro to 'Row Seven' began, you finally understood: some people take two whole years to walk from the seats to the stage — and every step is worth it. No call time, no cameras, no one waiting for either of you to be someone else.
lines.zh: 几万人的星海为你们亮起。那首《第七排》的前奏响起时，你终于明白：有些人从台下走到台上，走了整整两年，可每一步都值得。第七排的那个位子从此空着，因为坐在那里的人已经不必再买票了。

lines.en: The Show With an Audience of One
lines.zh: 只有你的那场演出

lines.en: He never returned to the arena stage, and he never missed it.
lines.zh: 他没有再回到万人舞台，也不觉得可惜。

lines.en: That tiny livehouse became his home turf. Fewer fans — but every one of them truly understood him.
lines.zh: 那间小小的livehouse成了他的主场。粉丝少了，但每一个都是真的懂他的人。

lines.en: You never made a grand public announcement, and never hid, either. At the end of every show he'd play a song he never named, then look toward one fixed spot in the crowd — row seven, always kept for you.
lines.zh: 你们没有大张旗鼓地公开，也没有刻意隐瞒。他会在每场演出的最后，弹一首没报过名的歌，然后看向台下固定的那个位置——第七排，永远为你留着。

lines.en: "Know which show is my favorite?" he asked one night after closing.
lines.zh: "你知道我最喜欢哪场演出吗？"有天散场后他问你。

lines.en: "Which one?"
lines.zh: "哪场？"

lines.en: He slung the guitar onto his back, leaned in, and grinned. "The ones I play just for you at home. Zero bad reviews." No call time, no cameras, no one waiting for either of you to be someone else.
lines.zh: 他把吉他往身后一背，凑近你，坏笑："回家给你一个人唱的那些。零差评。"第七排的那个位子从此空着，因为坐在那里的人已经不必再买票了。

lines.en: After the Lights Go Down
lines.zh: 散场之后

lines.en: The confession was quietly buried by the label; the official statement called it an improvised stage moment.
lines.zh: 那场告白后来被公司压了下去，官方声明说：那只是一个即兴的舞台桥段。

lines.en: You never appeared on any camera, and you never went back to row seven.
lines.zh: 你没有出现在任何镜头里，也再没去过第七排。

lines.en: He's still the top idol adored by millions, his smile still flawless. Only sometimes, on an encore, he looks toward one direction in the crowd, pauses for half a second, then carries on as if nothing happened.
lines.zh: 他依然是万人追捧的顶流，笑容依旧完美。只是偶尔在某场演唱会的安可，他会看向观众席某个方向，停顿半秒，然后若无其事地继续。

lines.en: Years later you still keep that row-seven ticket stub.
lines.zh: 很多年后你还留着那张第七排的票根。

lines.en: You once heard a song in its raw form — backstage at midnight, no lights, no makeup, just a convenience-store rice ball. That version, no one in the world heard but you. And that's enough. No call time, no cameras, no one waiting for either of you to be someone else.
lines.zh: 有些歌你曾经听过原声——在没有灯、没有妆、只有一根便利店饭团的深夜后台。那个版本，全世界只有你听过。这就够了。第七排的那个位子从此空着，因为坐在那里的人已经不必再买票了。
